questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v1`

### Contexto
A common pet that barks.

### Enunciado
What animal says "Woof woof"?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **dog** (perro) is known for the sound "Woof woof".

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v2`

### Contexto
A big animal that gives milk.

### Enunciado
What animal says "Moo"?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **cow** (vaca) makes the "Moo" sound and gives milk.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v3`

### Contexto
Describing animal movements.

### Enunciado
Which animal can **fly** in the sky?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Birds** (pájaros/aves) have wings and can fly.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v4`

### Contexto
Animal habitats.

### Enunciado
Where does a **Fish** live?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Fish** (peces) live in water (oceans, rivers, lakes).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v5`

### Contexto
Categorizing animals.

### Enunciado
Which of these is a **Farm Animal** (animal de granja)?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **pig** (cerdo) is commonly found on farms. Lions and monkeys are wild animals.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v6`

### Contexto
Identifying animals by characteristics.

### Enunciado
I have long ears and I like to hop (saltar). I love carrots. What am I?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Rabbits** (conejos) have long ears and eat carrots.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v7`

### Contexto
Plurals of animals.

### Enunciado
What is the correct plural of **Mouse**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Mouse" (ratón) has an irregular plural: **mice** (ratones).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v8`

### Contexto
Body parts of animals.

### Enunciado
Which animal has a **long trunk** (trompa larga)?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The **elephant** (elefante) uses its long trunk to breathe, drink, and grab things.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v9`

### Contexto
Analyzing diet.

### Enunciado
An animal that eats **only meat** is called a ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **carnivore** (carnívoro) is an animal that feeds on meat.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-animals-001-v10`

### Contexto
Life cycles (simple).

### Enunciado
A **Caterpillar** changes into a ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A caterpillar (oruga) undergoes metamorphosis to become a **butterfly** (mariposa).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v1`

### Contexto
The part of the body you use to see.

### Enunciado
Which part of your body do you use to **look** at a beautiful flower?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
We use our **eyes** (ojos) for seeing.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v2`

### Contexto
The part of the body you use to hear music.

### Enunciado
Which part of your body do you use to **listen** to your teacher?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
We use our **ears** (orejas/oídos) for hearing.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v3`

### Contexto
Parts of the face.

### Enunciado
Where is your **Nose** located?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The **nose** (nariz) is in the center of the face.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v4`

### Contexto
Movement and exercise.

### Enunciado
What part of your body do you use to **kick** a football?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
You use your **foot** (pie) to kick a ball.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v5`

### Contexto
Sentence completion.

### Enunciado
I have two ________ and two ________ to walk and run.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
We use **legs** (piernas) and **feet** (pies) for locomotion like walking and running.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v6`

### Contexto
Identifying body functions.
"I use my ________ to taste (saborear) my delicious lunch."

### Enunciado
Choose the correct part of the body.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
We use our **mouth** (boca) and tongue to eat and taste food.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v7`

### Contexto
Specific parts of the limbs.

### Enunciado
In my hands, I have ten ________. In my feet, I have ten ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
In English, "fingers" (dedos de la mano) and "toes" (dedos del pie) are different words.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v8`

### Contexto
Physical descriptions.
"The boy has long ________ and big ________."

### Enunciado
Which option best completes a description of hair and ears?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Hair" (cabello) can be long, and "ears" (orejas) can be big.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v9`

### Contexto
Hygiene and health.
"I use my ________ to brush my teeth."

### Enunciado
Wait, what do you use to **hold** the toothbrush?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
We use our **hand** (mano) to grasp and use tools like a toothbrush.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-body-001-v10`

### Contexto
Logical associations.

### Enunciado
Which of these is NOT on your **Head**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The **knee** (rodilla) is part of the leg. Hair, forehead (frente), and chin (mentón) are on the head.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v1`

### Contexto
What you wear on your torso (tronco).

### Enunciado
What do you call the piece of clothing you wear on your upper body?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **T-shirt** (camiseta) is worn on the upper part of the body.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v2`

### Contexto
What you wear on your legs.

### Enunciado
I have two long legs. What should I wear?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Pants** (pantalones) are worn to cover the legs.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v3`

### Contexto
Clothing for your feet.

### Enunciado
Before you put on your **Shoes**, you put on your ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
We wear **socks** (medias/calcetines) inside our shoes.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v4`

### Contexto
Accessories.

### Enunciado
What do you wear on your **Head** to protect you from the sun?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **cap** (gorra) or hat is worn on the head.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v5`

### Contexto
Matching clothes with weather.
"It is a very **Sunny** day at the beach."

### Enunciado
What is the best thing to wear?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **swimsuit** (traje de baño) is appropriate for sunny days at the beach.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v6`

### Contexto
Clothes for girls.

### Enunciado
Which piece of clothing is typically worn as one single piece by girls and women?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **dress** (vestido) is a one-piece garment.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v7`

### Contexto
Identifying pairs.

### Enunciado
Which of these items do you usually wear in **Pairs** (two)?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
We have two feet, so we use **shoes** and **socks** in pairs.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v8`

### Contexto
Compound nouns/Descriptions.
"In the winter, I wear a **Heavy Jacket**."

### Enunciado
Why do people wear a jacket?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **jacket** (chaqueta) is used for protection against the cold.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v9`

### Contexto
Color and Clothing adjectives.
"The girl is wearing a **blue skirt** and a **white blouse**."

### Enunciado
What color is the skirt?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The description says "blue skirt" (falda azul).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-clothes-001-v10`

### Contexto
Formal vs. Casual.

### Enunciado
Which item is usually part of a **School Uniform**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **shirt** (camisa) is a standard part of school uniforms.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v1`

### Contexto
Look at the fruit: **Apple**.

### Enunciado
What color is a typical ripe apple?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Red (rojo) is the primary color associated with apples.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v2`

### Contexto
Look at the sky on a sunny day.

### Enunciado
What color is the sky?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Blue (azul) is the color of a clear sky.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v3`

### Contexto
The Colombian flag has three colors.

### Enunciado
Which color is at the top of the Colombian flag?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The Colombian flag colors are Yellow (amarillo), Blue, and Red. Yellow is on top.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v4`

### Contexto
Mixing colors.

### Enunciado
If you mix **Blue** and **Yellow**, what color do you get?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Blue + Yellow = Green (verde).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v5`

### Contexto
Sentence completion.

### Enunciado
The grass is ________ and the sun is ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Grass is green (hierba verde) and the sun is usually depicted as yellow (sol amarillo).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v6`

### Contexto
Identify the object by color.

### Enunciado
I am a fruit. I am small, round, and my color is **Orange**. What am I?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The fruit "Orange" (naranja) has the same name as its color.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v7`

### Contexto
Reading a short description.
"My dog is **White** with **Black** spots. He has a **Brown** collar."

### Enunciado
What colors is the dog?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The dog is "White with Black spots". Brown is the color of the collar, not the dog.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v8`

### Contexto
Logical grouping.

### Enunciado
Which group contains only **Primary Colors**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The primary colors (colores primarios) are Red, Blue, and Yellow.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v9`

### Contexto
Completing a sequence or pattern.
"Red, Apple; Yellow, Banana; Green, ________; Purple, Grape."

### Enunciado
Choose the best word to complete the sequence.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The sequence matches a color with a fruit of that color. Green matches with "Pear" (pera).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-colors-001-v10`

### Contexto
Analyzing a Rainbow.

### Enunciado
How many colors are traditionally found in a rainbow?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A rainbow (arcoíris) is traditionally said to have seven colors (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v1`

### Contexto
The teacher wants the students to stop standing.

### Enunciado
What does the teacher say when it's time to work at your desk?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Sit down" (siéntate/siéntense) is the command used to ask students to take their seats.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v2`

### Contexto
The teacher wants the students to rise from their chairs.

### Enunciado
What is the command to get up from your seat?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Stand up" (ponte de pie / pónganse de pie) is the opposite of sit down.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v3`

### Contexto
Starting a reading activity.

### Enunciado
The teacher says: "________ your books to page ten."

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Open your books" (abran sus libros) is the instruction to start using the book.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v4`

### Contexto
Finishing a lesson.

### Enunciado
When the class is over, the teacher says: "________ your books, please."

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Close your books" (cierren sus libros) is the instruction when finishing an activity or the lesson.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v5`

### Contexto
Requesting attention/silence.
"Students are talking too much."

### Enunciado
What does the teacher say to ask for silence?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Be quiet" (silencio / guarda silencio) is used to manage classroom noise.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v6`

### Contexto
Following multi-step instructions.
"First, **Listen**. Second, **Repeat**."

### Enunciado
What should you do after the teacher speaks if they say "Repeat"?

### Options

options.text: Say the same words as the teacher

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Repeat" (repite / repitan) means to say again what has been heard.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v7`

### Contexto
Instructions for written work.

### Enunciado
If the teacher says "________ your name at the top of the paper", what should you do?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Write your name" (escribe tu nombre) is a common instruction for identification of work.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v8`

### Contexto
Interactive classroom actions.

### Enunciado
"Please, ________ to the board and draw a circle."

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Come to the board" (ven al tablero) is the invitation for a student to participate at the front of the room.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v9`

### Contexto
Comprehending negative commands.

### Enunciado
"Do **not** run in the classroom." This means:

### Options

options.text: You must walk slowly and carefully.
You must jump on the desks.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Do not run" (no corras) prohibits running for safety reasons, implying one should walk.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-commands-001-v10`

### Contexto
Identifying correct responses to instructions.
Teacher: "Raise your hand if you have a question."

### Enunciado
What is the student doing?

### Options

options.text: Lifting their arm to get the teacher's attention.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Raise your hand" (levanta la mano) is the standard way to ask permission to speak in a classroom.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v1`

### Contexto
The person who gave birth to you.

### Enunciado
Who is the female parent in a family?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The female parent is called the **mother** (madre).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v2`

### Contexto
A male sibling.

### Enunciado
Your parents' son is your ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A male sibling is called a **brother** (hermano).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v3`

### Contexto
The father of your father.

### Enunciado
Who is your father's father?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Your parent's father is your **grandfather** (abuelo).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v4`

### Contexto
Identifying family roles.

### Enunciado
My mother's sister is my ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The sister of your parent is your **aunt** (tía).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v5`

### Contexto
Possessive adjectives and family.
"This is Maria. She is my father's sister."

### Enunciado
Complete the sentence: Maria is my ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Father's sister" equals **aunt** (tía).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v6`

### Contexto
Sentence reconstruction.
"son / my / is / He / brother / my"

### Enunciado
Identify the correct meaning of this relationship: "He is my parents' son."

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The son of your parents is your **brother** (hermano).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v7`

### Contexto
Understanding extended family.
"My aunt's son is playing with me."

### Enunciado
The son of your aunt is your ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
An aunt's or uncle's child is called a **cousin** (primo/prima).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v8`

### Contexto
Family trees.
"My mother's mother has a birthday today."

### Enunciado
Who is having a birthday?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The mother of your mother is your **grandmother** (abuela).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v9`

### Contexto
Plurals and family groups.

### Enunciado
What is the correct way to refer to your **Mother** and **Father** together as one word?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
In English, "Mother and Father" are collectively called **parents** (padres). Note that "relatives" includes uncles, aunts, etc.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-family-001-v10`

### Contexto
Complex relationships.
"If I am a girl, I am my parents' ________."

### Enunciado
Choose the correct word.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A female child is the **daughter** (hija) of her parents.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v1`

### Contexto
You have a big smile on your face because you got a new toy!

### Enunciado
How do you feel?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A smile is a sign of being **happy** (feliz/contento).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v2`

### Contexto
You lost your favorite pencil and you want to cry.

### Enunciado
How do you feel?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Wanting to cry because of a loss is a sign of being **sad** (triste).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v3`

### Contexto
You didn't sleep well last night.

### Enunciado
"I am yawning (bostezando) a lot. I feel ________."

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Yawning is a sign of being **tired** (cansado).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v4`

### Contexto
You see a big, scary spider.

### Enunciado
How do you feel?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Seeing something scary makes you feel **scared** (asustado).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v5`

### Contexto
Physical feelings.
"I want to drink a big glass of water."

### Enunciado
I am ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A desire to drink water means you are **thirsty** (sediento/con sed).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v6`

### Contexto
Understanding emotions from situations.
"It is my birthday party today!"

### Enunciado
"I feel very ________!"

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A birthday party makes someone feel **excited** (emocionado).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v7`

### Contexto
Identifying opposites.

### Enunciado
What is the opposite of **Happy**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Sad** (triste) is the most direct opposite of **Happy** (feliz).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v8`

### Contexto
Physical temperature feelings.
"The weather is snowy (nevando) and the wind is freezing."

### Enunciado
How does the person feel?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Snow and freezing wind cause someone to feel **cold** (con frío).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v9`

### Contexto
Complex social feelings.
"I have nothing to do. No TV, no games, no books."

### Enunciado
I feel ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Having nothing interesting to do leads to feeling **bored** (aburrido).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-feelings-001-v10`

### Contexto
Analyzing physical needs.
"My stomach is making noise and I am thinking about pizza."

### Enunciado
I am ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Stomach noises and thinking about food mean you are **hungry** (hambriento).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v1`

### Contexto
A common yellow fruit.

### Enunciado
What fruit is long, yellow, and monkeys love it?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **banana** (banano/plátano) is yellow and often associated with monkeys.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v2`

### Contexto
A white drink from cows.

### Enunciado
What do we call the white liquid we drink or put in cereal?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Milk** (leche) is white and comes from cows.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v3`

### Contexto
Identifying vegetables.

### Enunciado
Which of these is a **Vegetable** (verdura)?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **carrot** (zanahoria) is a vegetable. Strawberries are fruit, and cookies are snacks.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v4`

### Contexto
Expressing likes. (I like / I don't like).
"I love sweet things. My favorite dessert is ________."

### Enunciado
Choose the best option for a sweet dessert.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Ice cream** (helado) is a common sweet dessert.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v5`

### Contexto
Categorizing food groups (Healthy vs. Unhealthy).

### Enunciado
Which group contains only **Healthy Food** (comida saludable)?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Apples, carrots, and water are healthy options compared to fast food or sweets.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v6`

### Contexto
Breakfast vocabulary.
"In the morning, I eat egg and ________ for breakfast."

### Enunciado
Choose the most common breakfast item.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Bread** (pan) is a staple breakfast item in many cultures.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v7`

### Contexto
Meals of the day.

### Enunciado
We eat **Breakfast** in the morning. When do we eat **Dinner**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Dinner (cena) is the meal typically eaten at night.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v8`

### Contexto
Understanding ingredients.
"To make a **Sandwich**, you usually need ________."

### Enunciado
Which ingredients are essential for a sandwich?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A sandwich is primarily made with **bread** and fillings like ham and cheese.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v9`

### Contexto
Food origins.

### Enunciado
Where does **Bread** come from?

### Options

options.text: It is made from flour (wheat) in a bakery.
It grows on trees in the forest.
It is found under the ground like carrots.
Animals like cows give us bread.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Bread is a processed food made from flour (harina), which comes from grains like wheat (trigo).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-food-001-v10`

### Contexto
Analyzing physical responses.
"My mouth is watering because I see a delicious pizza."

### Enunciado
This means I am ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Wanting to eat something delicious means you are **hungry** (hambriento / con hambre).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v1`

### Contexto
Waking up in the morning.

### Enunciado
What do you say to your teacher when you arrive at school at 7:00 AM?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Good morning" (buenos días) is used from sunrise until noon.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v2`

### Contexto
Saying goodbye.

### Enunciado
When you go home after school, what do you say to your friends?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Goodbye" (adiós) or "Bye" is used when leaving a place or person.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v3`

### Contexto
Meeting someone for the first time.

### Enunciado
What is the correct question to ask a new student about their **name**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"What is your name?" (¿Cómo te llamas?) is the standard way to ask for someone's identity.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v4`

### Contexto
Asking about well-being.

### Enunciado
If a friend asks "How are you?", what is a good answer?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"I am fine, thank you" (Estoy bien, gracias) is a polite response to being asked how you are.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v5`

### Contexto
Polite request (Magic words).
"Can you give me a pencil, ________?"

### Enunciado
Choose the most polite word to complete the sentence.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Please" (por favor) is the polite word used when asking for something.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v6`

### Contexto
Receiving something.
"Here is your notebook."
"________."

### Enunciado
What should you say after receiving your notebook?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Thank you" (gracias) is used to express gratitude.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v7`

### Contexto
Introduction sequence.
A: "Hello! I am Maria."
B: "Hi Maria! I am Juan. ________."

### Enunciado
What is a polite phrase to finish this introduction?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Nice to meet you" (mucho gusto / encantado de conocerte) is used after being introduced to someone.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v8`

### Contexto
Time of day greetings.
It is **3:00 PM** and you see your neighbor.

### Enunciado
What is the best greeting for this time?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Good afternoon" (buenas tardes) is used from noon until early evening (around 5:00-6:00 PM).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v9`

### Contexto
Social etiquette at night.
You are leaving a party at 9:00 PM to go to sleep.

### Enunciado
What is the correct way to say goodbye at night before sleeping?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Good night" (feliz noche / que descanses) is used specifically when leaving or going to bed at night. "Good evening" is for arriving.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-greetings-001-v10`

### Contexto
Replying to thanks.
A: "Thank you for the marker!"
B: "________."

### Enunciado
Choose the correct polite response.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"You're welcome" (de nada / con gusto) is the standard response to "Thank you".

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v1`

### Contexto
Counting fingers on one hand.

### Enunciado
How many fingers do you have on one hand?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
One hand has **five** (cinco) fingers.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v2`

### Contexto
Number sequence.
"1, 2, 3, ____, 5"

### Enunciado
What is the missing number?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The sequence follows the order of numbers: 1, 2, 3, **four** (cuatro), 5.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v3`

### Contexto
Addition (Sumas simples).
"Ten plus two equals ________"

### Enunciado
What is 10 + 2?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
10 + 2 = **twelve** (doce).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v4`

### Contexto
Spelling numbers.

### Enunciado
Which is the correct spelling for the number **15**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The correct spelling for 15 is **fifteen**. Note how it changes from "five".

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v5`

### Contexto
Age and social conversation.
"I am **9** years old. My sister is **7**."

### Enunciado
What is the total age of both siblings added together?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
9 + 7 = **sixteen** (dieciséis).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v6`

### Contexto
Count the animals.
"There are **eight** cats and **three** dogs in the park."

### Enunciado
How many animals are there in total?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
8 + 3 = **eleven** (once).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v7`

### Contexto
Counting objects in categories.
"Maria has **six** red pencils, **four** blue pencils, and **seven** yellow pencils."

### Enunciado
How many pencils does Maria have in total?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
6 + 4 + 7 = **seventeen** (diecisiete).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v8`

### Contexto
Comparing numbers.

### Enunciado
Which number is **greater than** (más grande que) thirteen and **less than** (menor que) fifteen?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The number between 13 (thirteen) and 15 (fifteen) is **fourteen** (catorce).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v9`

### Contexto
Multiplication (multiplicación básica) / Pattern.
"Two, Four, Six, Eight, ________"

### Enunciado
What number completes the sequence?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The sequence increases by 2 each time (even numbers). After 8 comes **ten** (diez).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-numbers-001-v10`

### Contexto
Understanding time/calendar.

### Enunciado
How many months are in **one year**?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
There are **twelve** (doce) months in a year.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v1`

### Contexto
The object you use to write.

### Enunciado
What object do you use to write with lead (grafito)?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **pencil** (lápiz) is used for writing or drawing.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v2`

### Contexto
The object you use to fix mistakes.

### Enunciado
If you make a mistake with a pencil, you use a ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
An **eraser** (borrador) is used to remove pencil marks.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v3`

### Contexto
Carrying your supplies.

### Enunciado
Where do you keep your books and notebooks when you go to school?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **backpack** (mochila/morral) is used to carry school supplies.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v4`

### Contexto
Using a ruler.

### Enunciado
What do you use to draw a straight line?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **ruler** (regla) is used to measure and draw lines.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v5`

### Contexto
Matching actions with objects.
"I need to cut this paper for my project."

### Enunciado
Which tool do I need?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
**Scissors** (tijeras) are used for cutting materials like paper.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v6`

### Contexto
Identifying furniture in the classroom.

### Enunciado
You sit on a ________ and you write on a ________.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
In a classroom, students sit on **chairs** (sillas) and use **desks** (pupitres/escritorios) to work.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v7`

### Contexto
Categorizing supplies.

### Enunciado
Which object is NOT used for writing or coloring?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A **sharpener** (sacapuntas) is used to sharpen pencils, but you cannot write with it directly.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v8`

### Contexto
Vocabulary in context.
"Teacher: Please open your ________ to page twenty."

### Enunciado
Complete the teacher's instruction.

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Instructing students to "open to a page" refers to using a **book** (libro).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v9`

### Contexto
Problem solving.
"Your pencil is broken and the tip (punta) is short."

### Enunciado
What do you need to do?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
When a pencil tip breaks, you use a **sharpener** to make it functional again.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-04-school-001-v10`

### Contexto
Classroom locations.

### Enunciado
Where does the teacher usually write for everyone to see?

### Options
questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The **board** (tablero/pizarra) is the central place where teachers write for the class.

---
